issues.quote: Aurèle was never the easiest man to speak well of.
issues.fact: The fact sheet never mentions Monnier or identifies the dead man. The transcript never states that Aurèle, the host, is Monnier, the victim.
issues.misreading: A solver could take Aurèle and Monnier as two different men, so the dead man might be someone other than Aurèle, or the 'his' in the 'repeater' and 'regulator' passages might point to a different person. That would change whose watch and clocks the doctor is describing.

issues.quote: I can tell you the regulator on the wall had stopped. Stopped with its master, I thought.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no reading for any stopped clock, and the transcript gives no time for when the regulator stopped.
issues.misreading: A solver could treat the stopped wall regulator as a clock reading that fixes the time of death, which the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: When I saw him, he was already dead, and there was nothing a doctor can do.
issues.fact: The sheet says nothing about when or where the doctor saw the body.
issues.misreading: Because this answer comes right after the hall and piano exchange, a solver could infer that the doctor found the body during his trip to the hall, which places Monnier in the hall during the 15-minute absence.

issues.quote: He meant it to strike the new century for him, the way a man wants to have the last word.
issues.fact: The sheet mentions no repeater and gives no setting or chime reading for it.
issues.misreading: A solver could read the repeater's set chime as an extra timing reading, for example that it was set to strike midnight and could fix the time of death.

issues.quote: It strikes its own hours from its own face and does not wait for anyone's permission.
issues.fact: The sheet only says the hall clock struck eleven a moment after the player sat down again. It makes no claim about the clock's accuracy.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as a hint that the hall clock is unsynchronized with the watches and so not a reliable reference for the eleven o'clock reading.

issues.quote: Death would have been very quick.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no information about how long death took.
issues.misreading: A solver could infer that the blow was struck shortly before the doctor arrived, which would narrow the time of death without a basis in the sheet.
